question: Which telescope was invented by Isaac Newton in the 17th century by using a concave mirror to collect light instead of a simple lens which produces false colours due to the dispersion of light?
solution:
The correct answer is __**reflecting telescope.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reflecting telescope:-**

 
 
• ​It was invented by Isaac Newton in the 17th century.
 
• This telescope uses a concave mirror to collect and reflect light, which eliminates the problem of false colours that occur due to the dispersion of light in a simple lens.
 
• Reflecting telescopes are widely used in modern astronomy and are used to study celestial objects such as stars, galaxies, and planets.
 
• The first reflecting telescope was built by James Gregory in the 17th century, before Newton's version.
 
• The reflecting telescope is also known as a Newtonian telescope and has a wide range of applications in astronomy and astrophysics.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Infrared telescope:-**

 
 
• It uses infrared radiation to detect objects in space.
 
 
 
• **Monocular telescope:-**
 
 
• It is a small, handheld telescope used for terrestrial observation.
 
 
 
• **Graphic telescope:-**
 
 
• It is not a commonly used term in astronomy or optics.
